svg.title: Why SSM is the modern default: the whole complexity of PIM-SM exists because the source is unknown
svg.desc: A decision flow at the top: do receivers know the source address in advance? If yes, use SSM in 232/8 with IGMPv3 - no RP, no shared tree, no register, state is (S,G) only. If no, one of two ASM cases applies: many senders with many receivers use bidirectional PIM with a single (*,G) per group, and a few senders with a large audience use PIM-SM with an RP. Below, four deployment patterns are matched to the answer: an IPTV head-end with fixed encoder addresses goes SSM, a trading floor with a fixed feed list goes SSM, a video conference with anyone as sender stays ASM, and market data fan-out from many publishers uses bidirectional PIM. A bottom band lists the price of SSM: the application must know the source, IGMPv3 must be end to end, and 232/8 must be reachable on every hop.
svg.text: The real question is not "which protocol". It is "does the receiver know the source"
Answer yes and the RP, the shared tree, the register and half the failure modes disappear from the design.
Does the receiver know
the source address?
before it sends the join
YES -> SSM
232/8, IGMPv3 include mode, (S,G) only.
No RP, no register, no shared tree, no switchover.
NO -> ASM, then pick the shape
Many senders, many receivers: bidirectional PIM.
Few senders, large audience: PIM-SM with an RP.
The RP is a workaround for "I do not know
who is sending". If you do know, you are
paying for a workaround you do not need.
This single question removes more design
risk than any tuning knob in PIM.
ip pim ssm default / ssm range 232/8
FOUR REAL DEPLOYMENTS, FOUR ANSWERS
IPTV head-end
Encoder addresses are fixed and
documented. Receivers are STBs
with a channel list.
SSM, no RP at all
Trading floor
Each feed has one publisher and
a fixed distribution list.
Latency budget is milliseconds.
SSM, plus PIM on the LAN
Video conference
Anyone can be a sender, and the
receiver cannot know who in
advance.
ASM or application-level MCU
Market data fan-out
Many publishers, many consumers,
no fixed pairing, tree shape is
nearly symmetric.
BiDir-PIM, one (*,G)
WHAT SSM COSTS YOU
The application must know the source
A channel list, a manifest, a discovery service.
If it cannot, SSM mapping is a patch, not a design.
IGMPv3 must run end to end
One IGMPv2 hop downgrades the join to (*,G)
and the RP comes back into your life.
232/8 must be routed everywhere
Missing it on one hop is a black hole with
no error message, exactly like a missing RP.
